summary: Iteration 14 (Late Arrival + Undo) verified end-to-end. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter14.py (7 tests, ALL PASSING) covering: (1) /api/stats persons=71/details=71/lines=15 (new file); (2) baseline generation for 2026-08-19 day X-Smart p=1 rc=1 + Element 2 p=2 rc=1 with 1 absent from X-Smart P&C; (3) POST /schedule/{date}/late-arrival WITHOUT target returns {person, best_fit, planned[], not_planned[]}; planned entries all reference active lines, not_planned entries reference inactive lines, all filtered by person's skills; (4) POST /schedule/{date}/late-arrival WITH target on a planned cell at required: pid removed from absent_person_ids, assigned to the target cell, and either 'displaced_placed_id' is set (auto-reassigned to a skill-matching shortage cell) or 'displaced' conflict object is returned with an options[] list; (5) POST /schedule/{date}/undo restores previous absent_person_ids and clears previous_state so the next undo returns 400; (6) POST /schedule/{date}/late-arrival WITH target on NOT-PLANNED line correctly appends that line to line_configs at max_prio+1 with run_count=1 and generates the schedule with the person assigned to the added cell; (7) 400 for missing person_id, 404 for unknown person. Frontend Playwright flow on /board?date=2026-08-19&shift=day: located exactly one late-arrival-<id> button on the absent chip (Dharmila Vasava); clicking opened late-arrival-dialog with late-arrival-best banner and late-arrival-approve button; clicking Approve invoked API; when auto-reassignment was not possible, conflict-dialog opened; toolbar undo-btn is present and functional (toast 'Undone' shown, absent chip restored). No regressions observed in schedule shape, absent chip, unassigned pool, or toolbar controls.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py late_arrival (L810-983) correctly snapshots the pre-mutation state (line_configs, absent_person_ids, overrides, unassigned_keys, required_overrides) BEFORE calling generate_schedule, and persists the snapshot in $set after the new schedule is stored — undo path (L986-1008) rebuilds from that snapshot and clears it, guaranteeing one-step undo semantics. Second undo returns 400 as spec'd.

Displacement heuristic (L917-918): current_ids.sort(key=lambda i: -skill_totals.get(i,0)) then pop(0) actually keeps the MOST-specialized worker in place and displaces the LEAST-specialized (highest skill_total sorted first, pop from index 0). Comment at L916 says 'displace LAST-in' but implementation is actually 'least-specialized first' which matches spec — recommend updating the comment for clarity.

Auto-reassignment loop for displaced worker (L931-946) iterates over sched_doc['assignments'] (the OLD schedule) rather than the just-updated cells, meaning shortages are read pre-displacement. This is acceptable because the target cell is explicitly skipped and other cells' shortages haven't changed, but note that if the same worker was multiply-assigned this could theoretically double-place; not observed in practice since generate_schedule dedups downstream.

OptionRow testid pattern `late-planned-${o.line}-${o.detail}` and `conflict-opt-${o.line}-${o.detail}` include spaces (e.g. 'X-Smart P & C'); selectors using CSS attribute matching will need proper escaping — recommend documenting for future test authors (data-testid attribute selectors need [data-testid="..."] quoting).

BoardPage.jsx L373 fallback template `${lateArr.person.name} ${lateArr.person.surname}` is a defensive backstop; the primary path uses only lateArr.person.name which is what the backend returns from _person_full_name — consistent behavior.
